THE WELLINGTON WAVE
2026 Weekly Edition · Regular-Season Finale · July 20
Undefeated Division 2 Champions · 5–0

A Perfect
Finish

Wellington closes an undefeated Division 2 season with a 305–191 win, four team records and 13 new qualifying spots.

Wellington
305
—
Windsor Forest
191

The Wellington Waves finished the regular season the same way they started it: with a win.

Wellington defeated Windsor Forest 305–191 on July 20 to complete a perfect 5–0 Division 2 season. It was the Waves’ second undefeated Division 2 finish in three years, matching their 5–0 record from 2024.

After a difficult season in Division 1 last summer, Wellington returned to Division 2 and won all five of its scored dual meets in 2026. The Waves finished ahead of Windsor Forest, Edgehill, Williamsburg Community, Powhatan Secondary and West Point.

And they saved some of their biggest swims for the final Monday night of the regular season.

The meet produced four new Wellington team records, 13 new qualifying spots and season-best performances throughout the roster.

Among the League’s Fastest

Sophia Burnette delivered one of Wellington’s strongest league-wide swims of the night. Her 18.75 in the Girls 7–8 25-meter freestyle ranked third across VPSU. She also recorded a season-best 23.25 in backstroke and had already qualified for championships in both events.

Her performance was part of a much broader Wellington presence in the league rankings, with Waves swimmers appearing throughout the VPSU Top 50 across age groups and events.

Depth in the 11–12s

Wyatt Childress posted three VPSU top-10 performances in the same meet: sixth in the 50-meter freestyle, sixth in the 50-meter butterfly and seventh in the 100-meter individual medley.

Luke Shnowske ranked seventh in Boys 11–12 freestyle, while Grey Childress placed ninth in Girls 11–12 backstroke. It was not just one standout swim; Wellington had multiple swimmers competing near the front of the league across several events.

Still Getting Faster

The season finale produced 96 swimmer-event season bests, with every Wellington age group contributing.

Peyton Fidler dropped 13.69 seconds in the Boys 11–12 butterfly. Grey Childress recorded season bests in both backstroke and the individual medley, giving her best times in all five of her individual events by the end of the regular season.
